summary: A site for a band, musician, DJ or performer built around the new release and the tour: tour dates with ticket states, a discography with tracklists, videos, merch and a mailing list for presale codes.

pages.purpose: Lead with the act and the newest release, show the next dates, and turn visitors into listeners, ticket buyers and list subscribers.

sections.purpose: A full-bleed live or press photo with the name set edge to edge, the new release and the next show, and actions for tickets and listening.
fields: Hero photo with a real description as alt text
New release title, format and date
Primary action (tickets / pre-order) and secondary (watch / listen)
sections.notes: Make sure text over the photo keeps contrast (scrim). A running list of tour cities under the hero is a nice poster touch: it must pause on request and stop under reduced motion.

sections.purpose: The new or latest release: sleeve, release date, tracklist and where to pre-order or stream.
fields: Release title and kind (album, EP, single)
sections.notes: External store and streaming links open in a new tab and say so to screen readers.

sections.purpose: The next few dates with their ticket state and a link to the full tour page.
alternatives: list-layout: a simple dated list when only a handful of shows are announced
fields: Ticket state (on sale, few left, moved, sold out)
sections.notes: Show the state as text, not colour only. Group by month on the full page; here just the next five or six.

sections.purpose: Music videos and live sessions: one player and a list that swaps which video plays.
alternatives: media-text: a single featured video beside its description
fields: Year or context (official video, live session)
sections.notes: Click-to-load facade: nothing loads from the video host until play is pressed (privacy and speed).

sections.purpose: A few merch items with price and where to buy.
alternatives: gallery-section: merch photos linking to an external store

sections.purpose: Join the list for presale codes and news, choosing the nearest city so codes go to the right people.
alternatives: cta: a plain signup band without the city choice
fields: What subscribers get and how often
sections.notes: The result is a status region; explicit consent wording and a link to the privacy notice next to the button.

pages.purpose: Every date, grouped by month, filterable by region, with tickets, waitlists for sold-out shows and the practical answers fans need.

sections.purpose: Tour name, number of shows, support acts and age policy.
All dates grouped by month with region filter and 'hide sold out'.
fields: Per show: date, doors, city, country, venue, region, support, price, ticket state, ticket link
For moved shows: the original date
sections.notes: States: on sale, few left (primary button), new date (old date struck through and explained in text), sold out (ticket link replaced by a 'join waitlist' toggle with aria-pressed). A live count of shown dates; the waitlist result is announced.

sections.purpose: Waitlist rules, accessibility of venues, stage times, moved dates and refunds.
fields: How the waitlist and returns work
Refund and exchange rules for moved shows

pages.purpose: The discography: filter by kind, pick a sleeve and see its tracklist and links; then the band.

sections.purpose: What has been released so far.
A strip of sleeves with a kind filter; the chosen release shows its date, label, tracklist and listening links.
fields: Per release: title, kind, date, label, cover art, tracklist with durations, links; upcoming flag
sections.notes: Tracklist table with a visually hidden caption; upcoming releases get a badge and a pre-order action.

pages.purpose: Booking, press and management contacts, plus a press kit.

sections.purpose: Separate addresses for booking, press, management and label.
An enquiry form with the kind of request.

content: Act name and a short bio
Hero and press photos with credits and real alt text
Latest release: title, kind, date, cover, tracklist, formats, pre-order and streaming links
Back catalogue with the same details per release
Tour dates: date, doors, city, country, venue, support, price, ticket link and current ticket state
Waitlist, refund and moved-show policy; venue accessibility notes; age policy
Video links or files with poster images
Merch items with photos, prices, variants and store link (if selling)
Mailing list: what is sent, how often, presale lead time

styles.name: loud poster
styles.why: Dark, compact, a heavy lower-case display face with italic serif emphasis and one hot accent; tilting merch cards and a running city ticker. Suits indie, pop and electronic acts.

styles.name: quiet record sleeve
styles.why: Paper-light, serif and restrained, letting cover art and photos supply the colour. Suits jazz, classical, folk and singer-songwriters.

pitfalls: Ticket state shown by colour alone; 'sold out', 'few left' and 'new date' must be written, and moved shows must show both dates.
Out-of-date tour lists: past dates should drop off or move to an archive automatically.
Embedding video players that load third-party trackers on page load; use a click-to-load facade and mention it in the privacy notice.
Mailing-list signup without explicit consent, a privacy link or a clear cadence.
Text over a busy hero photo without a scrim fails contrast; placeholder alt text left on the hero photo.
Auto-moving tickers or animations with no pause control and no reduced-motion fallback.
External ticket and store links that open a new tab without saying so.
